concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI requires provenance metadata (`source_metadata.yaml`) to reside under the project‑level `data/` directory. T001 creates `code/data/...` and places the metadata file in `code/data/source_metadata.yaml`, violating the Materials Database Provenance rule.

Spec Edge Case 5 mandates a fallback sequence (Bulk → Shear → Formation Energy) when no bulk modulus is available. T002’s description only fetches data and never implements this fallback logic, dropping a required acceptance criterion.

The plan and Constitution III expect raw, processed, and result artifacts under top‑level `data/` and `results/`. T004 writes under `code/data/results/`, breaking the prescribed project structure and data‑hygiene conventions.

FR‑004 specifies training models for four residual targets (Bulk, Young’s, Shear, Poisson). T005 only mentions training for Residual Bulk Modulus (and “other residual moduli where available”) without guaranteeing all four targets, thus weakening the functional requirement.

The `output.schema.yaml` contract defines `sensitivity_analysis` fields as Type I error rates, but T006’s verification expects permutation‑test p‑values and variance. This mismatch will cause schema validation to fail, effectively weakening SC‑002/SC‑003.
Data‑hygiene (Constitution III) requires that all raw and processed datasets live under the top‑level `data/` directory. T003 outputs `code/data/processed/...`, violating this rule.

FR‑002 allows direct‑target models (including Miedema features) for comparative purposes, yet no task creates or evaluates such models, thereby discarding an allowed capability and narrowing the functional scope.
